components.css: .ds-steps { display: flex; gap: 4px; font-family: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-steps button { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 16px 0 7px; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; color: #34504c; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-steps button:hover { background: #f2f4ef; } .ds-steps b { display: grid; width: 30px; height: 30px; place-items: center; border-radius: 50%; background: #e6ebe4; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px #fff, inset 0 -2px 3px #0c2b291f; font-size: 14px; } .ds-steps button[aria-current='step'] { background: #f3b443; color: #17302e; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 1px #ffffff8c, inset 0 -5px 9px #7a4a0a33; } .ds-steps button[aria-current='step'] b { background: #17302e; color: #fdf8ee; }

narrative.overview:
Everything a future builder sees should look like someone made it at a kitchen table: pictures modelled in clay, controls pressed out of clay, reading laid on cut paper. The landing stands on a deep potter's-slip teal with a small clay town on an island in the harbour; every group on the board has its own piece of that town, and there is an empty plot for a group you bring. The working pages (Brief, Make & try, Your record) are pale paper, so the reading is calm, but the clay still turns up in the step discs, the photo frames and the empty state.

The point of the look is the product's point: this is people making useful things for people near them, not software issuing tasks. Warmth comes from material and colour, never from exclamation, sparkle or "magic" AI imagery. Density is generous: one decision per block, one problem per row.
keyCharacteristics: Real SVG lighting for clay (`ac-clay`, `ac-clay-flat`, `ac-clay-sm` in `src/Clay.tsx`), lit from the top left like a model on a table by a window.
A chunky rolled-clay display face over a highly legible reading face.
Teal ground for arriving, paper ground for working.
Marigold is the thing you press.
Cards sit a little off square on a sheet of their group's colour.

rules.name: The One Marigold Rule
rules.body: Each screen has one marigold action that matters most. A second marigold button on the same view means one of them should be quiet.

rules.name: The Group Colour Rule
rules.body: A group's colour comes from its piece of the town (`TINTS` in `src/Town.tsx`) and is used only as the paper its card sits on and the panel behind its piece. It never colours text or buttons.

rules.name: The Small Labels Stay Plain Rule
rules.body: Caprasimo is for 19px and up. Anything smaller, including small headings inside the record preview, uses Atkinson Hyperlegible at 700.

rules.name: The No Italic Display Rule
rules.body: Caprasimo has no italic. Emphasis in headlines is colour (marigold on teal, teal on paper), never a slanted face.

rules.name: The Real Clay Rule
rules.body: If it is meant to look modelled, draw it in SVG and give it `filter="url(#ac-clay)"` (or `ac-clay-sm` under 64px). Don't fake clay with stacked CSS gradients. Mount `<ClayDefs/>` once per page; the downloaded record has no defs, so anything shared with the record must not depend on the filter.

dos: Do draw anything meant to look modelled as SVG under the clay filter.
Do keep one marigold action per view.
Do keep problems in the group's own words, one per row.
Do show the honest label that the groups are made up, on the board and in the footer.
Do check every new screen at 390px and 320px with long text in the fields.
donts: Don't use sparkles, asterisks, glowing gradients or any "magic" AI imagery.
Don't use exclamation marks or em dashes in copy.
Don't set Caprasimo below 19px or in italic.
Don't put a small label above a heading. Let the heading say it.
Don't colour text or buttons with a group's tint.
